summary: This bill makes it unlawful for federal elected officials, congressional and executive employees, and political appointees to buy, sell, or trade prediction market contracts on government policy, actions, or political outcomes if they possess or could reasonably obtain material nonpublic information relevant to the trade.

scores.thoughts: The bill prohibits federal officials and employees from trading prediction market contracts on government policy or actions when using nonpublic information. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures or budgets.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or tax treatment of any financial instruments.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance markets, public coverage, or private healthcare systems.
The bill does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content relates to immigration policy, border enforcement, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill makes no reference to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense spending levels, or armed forces policy.
The legislation does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource protections.
No sections deal with welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
The bill contains nothing related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions concern drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill creates a new prohibition on certain financial transactions by officials but does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
Nothing in the text relates to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill does not authorize spending, alter deficits, or prioritize debt reduction.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The legislation makes no reference to foreign assistance or international aid programs.
While the bill restricts officials from trading prediction contracts on political outcomes, it does not change voting procedures, access, voter ID requirements, or election administration rules.
The bill regulates the conduct of government officials rather than imposing or relaxing rules on technology platforms or data privacy.
No content addresses worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
